lessons.title: Abraham’s Intercession
lessons.theme: Intercession is standing within God’s heart and pleading with him for others

v: Abraham came near, and said, “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?

May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”

lessons.still: Quietly picture yourself, like Abraham, “coming near” into God’s presence. Bring no needs of your own, only one person’s name. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I have come before you for them.”
teach: A child runs to his father and says, “Dad, my little brother knows he was wrong. Could you give him one more chance?” The child dares to say this because he knows his father’s heart. It was the same when Abraham interceded for Sodom: God first told him what he was about to do, and Abraham “came near” and pleaded with God for the city.

Abraham’s intercession has three marks. He “came near”: intercession is an act of drawing close to God. He pleaded on the basis of God’s character: “Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?” And he was humble yet persistent, going down from fifty to ten, each time setting himself aside and asking once more. Sodom was destroyed in the end, yet God “remembered Abraham” and brought Lot out.

Intercession is not persuading a reluctant God; it is stepping into God’s heart and working together with him. The more Abraham interceded, the better he came to know God’s justice and mercy. It is the same for us: intercession is God inviting us to stand beside him and care for this world together with him.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Intercession is praying for others, not for ourselves; it is the prayer of the self-emptied life. The focus is not on my own needs but on God’s heart and the salvation of others. Interceding humbly and persistently is letting Jesus reign in our prayers and taking part in building God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God told Abraham what he was about to do. What does that show you about how he regards those who intercede?
Who am I? — In your prayers, how does what you ask for yourself compare with what you ask for others?
How shall I respond? — For which “city” — your family, your workplace, your neighbourhood — will you come near and intercede?
lessons.jesus: Abraham interceded for Sodom down to ten righteous people; Jesus went further. He himself became the Righteous One who died in the place of sinners. He did not only intercede for the city; he personally bore the judgment the city deserved.
lessons.pray: Judge of all the earth, you are just and full of mercy. Teach me to come near like Abraham and intercede for my family, my colleagues and this city. I come before you not on my own merits but in the name of Jesus; have mercy, and let the lost be saved. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of three people or places you will keep praying for
Today, pray specifically for five minutes for a friend or relative who does not yet believe
Start an “intercession log” page in your prayer journal
lessons.noon: “Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?” — Lord, right now I ask your mercy on the city where I live.

lessons.title: Standing in the Gap
lessons.theme: An intercessor is the person God looks for at the breach

v: Moses returned to the LORD, and said, “Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made themselves gods of gold.
Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin— and if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written.”
“I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I would not destroy it; but I found no one.

lessons.still: Quietly stand up, or picture yourself standing before a gap in a wall. Say to the Lord, “Lord, you are looking for someone. Here I am.” Then ask him to show you where there is a breach around you.
teach: When a crack appears in a levee and no one plugs it, the flood will sweep away the whole village. City walls in ancient times were the same: a single breach was where the enemy would break in. In Ezekiel God says, “I sought for a man among them who would… stand in the gap.” God was looking for an intercessor, but “found no one.”

Moses was one who stood in the gap. The people worshipped the golden calf and committed a great sin. Moses did not make excuses for them; he admitted, “this people have sinned a great sin.” But then he said, “Yet now, if you will, forgive their sin—and if not, please blot me out of your book.” He placed himself between the people and judgment, preferring to be blotted out himself rather than see the people destroyed.

Standing in the gap is not pointing out other people’s faults; it is carrying their burdens. When we see breaches in our families, churches and society, our first reaction is often to criticise and complain. But God invites us not just to stand outside the wall pointing fingers, but to step into the breach and shield them in prayer.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The focus is not on other people’s faults, but on whether I will stand before God for them. Criticism is self-rule, standing on high ground to judge; intercession is self-emptying, stepping into the breach to carry the load. Humility draws out humility; those who stand in the gap are repairing the walls for God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God “sought for a man.” What does that show you about how unwilling he is for people to perish?
Who am I? — Faced with the breaches around you, do you more often criticise or intercede?
How shall I respond? — For which breach will you stand before God every day this week?
lessons.jesus: Moses said, “blot me out,” but God did not grant it. Jesus, though, truly was forsaken by the Father, so that our names could be written in the book of life. He is the ultimate one who stood in the gap, closing with his own body the rift between God’s judgment and human sin.
lessons.pray: Lord, you are looking for someone to stand in the gap, and I want to say: here I am. Forgive me for so often criticising and so seldom interceding. Today I stand before you for my family, my church and my nation; have mercy, bring revival, and repair every broken wall. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Turn a person or group you often criticise into someone you pray for
Pray for ten minutes about the biggest breach in your family right now
Agree with a spiritual companion to pray together about one matter this week
lessons.noon: “I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall” — Lord, right now I am willing to stand in the gap for others.

lessons.title: Jesus Intercedes for Us
lessons.theme: Our intercession rests on Jesus’ unceasing intercession

v: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
Therefore he is also able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for them.

lessons.still: Listen quietly: right now, at this very moment, Jesus is at the Father’s right hand praying for you. You don’t need to say anything; just receive this fact. Let the words “he is praying for me” sink slowly to the bottom of your heart.
teach: Waking in the night as a child and hearing your parents in the next room softly praying for you is a sense of safety you remember for life. John 17 lets us “overhear” Jesus’ prayer. On the night he was betrayed, he prayed not only for the disciples in front of him but also “for those also who will believe in me through their word.” You and I are in that prayer.

Jesus’ intercession has clear content: keep them from the evil one, sanctify them by the truth, make them one, so that the world may believe. Hebrews goes further: he “lives forever to make intercession for them.” Jesus’ intercession did not end at the cross. Today he is still interceding for us before the Father, and that is why he is able to “save to the uttermost.”

This changes the foundation of our intercession. We are not lonely prayer warriors; we are joining a prayer that has long been under way. When I intercede for others, I am following the heart of Jesus our High Priest. And this lets us rest: even when my prayers are weak, his intercession never stops.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Jesus is my example, even in intercession, where I follow him. His prayer for the disciples’ unity is the very heart of building God’s kingdom system. Our intercession does not depend on our own zeal or how long we pray, but on Jesus’ name and his intercession, so all the glory goes to him.
q: Who is God? — Jesus “lives forever to make intercession.” What does that tell you about his love for you?
Who am I? — Knowing that Jesus is praying for you, what burden can you lay down today?
How shall I respond? — Following Jesus’ heart, which brothers and sisters will you pray for to be one?
lessons.jesus: Before Peter denied him three times, Jesus told him, “I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.” Jesus’ intercession held Peter up not only while he stood but even more when he fell, and it prepared a calling for him once he turned back.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that right now you are praying for me before the Father. When I am weak, when I fall, even when I forget to pray, your intercession never stops. Bring my prayers into step with your heart, so that I pray for my brothers and sisters to be kept, made holy and made one, and the world may believe in you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Read John 17 and circle what Jesus asks for his disciples
Using the content of Jesus’ prayer, intercede for each member of your small group
Pray for a brother or sister who is stumbling, and send them a word of encouragement
lessons.noon: “he lives forever to make intercession for them” — Lord, right now thank you for interceding for me.

lessons.title: Praying for Those in Authority
lessons.theme: Our intercession must stretch wide enough to include all people and all in authority

v: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,
for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.
Seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive, and pray to the LORD for it; for in its peace you will have peace.”

lessons.still: Quietly imagine looking down from a height on the city where you live: its streets, schools, hospitals, government offices. Say to the Lord, “Lord, this city is yours; please give it peace.” Then bring to mind the name of one person in authority.
teach: If the passengers on a ship do nothing but complain about the captain and no one prays for him, the complaining won’t make the ship any safer. When Paul wrote, the power in charge was the Roman Empire, which often persecuted Christians, yet he said, “first of all” pray for “all men,” “for kings and all who are in high places.” This is not a political position; it is a heavenly perspective.

Paul says the purpose of this intercession is “that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence,” and the deeper reason is that God “desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.” Jeremiah, too, told the exiles in Babylon to seek the peace of the very city that had destroyed their homes. God’s people are not bystanders in society; they are watchmen in prayer.

Praying for those in authority does not mean approving of everything they do; it means acknowledging that ultimate authority is in God’s hands. Shift your perspective from “they decide my situation” to “God holds their hearts.” Then we need not be cynical, nor simply drift with the current; instead we keep watch over the land in prayer.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The kingdom, the power and the glory all belong to God. Praying for those in authority is praying the Lord’s Prayer: “Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth.” Our focus is on Jesus, not on our circumstances; letting Jesus reign over our nation and our city is our true hope.
q: Who is God? — God “desires all people to be saved.” What does that show you about how wide his heart is?
Who am I? — Toward those in authority over you, do you more often complain or intercede?
How shall I respond? — Which person in authority (in government, at work, at school) will you pray for specifically?
lessons.jesus: Standing before Pilate, Jesus said, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above.” He saw clearly the true sovereignty behind earthly power. He did not curse those who sentenced him to death; instead, on the cross he prayed for them: “Father, forgive them.”
lessons.pray: King of kings, I pray for the leaders of my nation, the officials of my city, the managers at my workplace, and the teachers in our schools. Give them wisdom and justice, so that we may live godly, upright and peaceful lives. Above all, let all people be saved and come to know the truth; may your kingdom come to this land. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray once for your nation’s leader and once for the head of your city
Ask for one specific blessing for your direct manager or your teacher
When you watch the news, turn one piece of bad news into a prayer
lessons.noon: “Seek the peace of the city” — Lord, right now I ask for peace for my city and its leaders.

lessons.title: Intercession Changes the Intercessor
lessons.theme: As I pray for others, God is changing me

v: The LORD restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

lessons.still: Think of someone who once hurt or misunderstood you. Be still for a moment. You don’t need to force any feeling; simply tell the Lord honestly, “Lord, I choose to pray for them.” Then say their name and ask the Lord to bless them.
teach: It has been said that it is hard to pray sincerely for someone while continuing to hate them. Intercession is like a window: we open it so that God’s light can shine into someone else’s life, only to discover that the first person lit up is the one standing at the window.

Job’s three friends wounded him with bad theology, yet God told them to ask Job to pray for them. The text says, “Yahweh restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends.” The turning point did not come when Job prayed for himself, but when he interceded for those who had hurt him. James also says, “pray for one another, that you may be healed.” Intercession is healing that flows both ways.

This week we have gone from Abraham, to Moses, to Jesus, to praying for all people, and now we come back to ourselves. As intercessors stand in the gap for others, their own hearts are enlarged, healed and changed into the likeness of Jesus. Next week we will learn to discern the Holy Spirit’s guidance, and prayer is exactly where we hear his voice.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Praying for those who have hurt me is the deepest practice of the self-emptied life. Pride provokes pride and both sides lose; intercession draws out humility and both sides win. When I intercede for my “2,” God produces the fruit of the Spirit in me, and the relationship is renewed as well.
q: Who is God? — God restored Job as he prayed for his friends. What does that show you about how God heals people?
Who am I? — Who is the hardest person for you to pray for?
How shall I respond? — Are you willing to pray for that person once a day this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus taught, “love your enemies… and pray for those who… persecute you,” and he lived it himself. As the nails went through his hands and feet, he said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Intercession kept him living in love even in the deepest wound.
lessons.pray: Lord, you tell me to pray for those who persecute me. I admit this is hard, but I choose to obey. Today I bless those who have hurt me; please heal the pain and bitterness in my heart too. Change me as I intercede, so that I become more and more like Jesus, who prayed for others on the cross. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask for one specific blessing for someone who has hurt you
Share a need with a spiritual companion and pray for each other
Write down what God has changed in your heart through intercession this week
lessons.noon: “when he prayed for his friends” — Lord, right now I pray to you for the person who is hard for me to love.
